title: Implement DVB-T2 §6.1.4 bit-to-cell-word demuxer
description:
## Goal

Implement ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §6.1.4 "Demultiplexing of bits into cell words" so that the existing TP06→TP07a chain validation (`4cdaf1c5`) can verify forward bit-exact agreement with the published ETSI test vectors.

## Context (block diagram per ETSI reference-streams documentation)

```
... LDPC 6 → Bit Interleaver → TP7 → Bit-to-cell Demux → TP7a → QAM Mapper → TP8 → ...
```

TP7a is the output of §6.1.4. The §6.1.4 stage demultiplexes the bit-interleaver output (`N` bits) into `N / η_MOD` cell words of `η_MOD` bits each, where `η_MOD` is the modulation order (2 for QPSK, 4 for 16-QAM, 6 for 64-QAM).

The 4cdaf1c5 worker's empirical analysis on 6 in-scope ETSI vectors showed ~50% diff rate between bit-interleaver-only output and TP07a, which matches the expected diff rate for ETSI's §6.1.4 sub-stream demux (output bit `k` corresponds to input bit at `substream * (N / η_MOD) + cell_index` where `substream = k mod η_MOD`, `cell_index = k / η_MOD`). So §6.1.4 alone should close the TP07a gap; §6.1.5 (cell interleaver, TP10) is downstream and out of scope here.

## Deliverables

1. New module: `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/cell_word_demux.rs`.

2. Public type, e.g. `DvbT2CellWordDemux`, with at minimum:
   - `pub fn new(modulation: DvbT2Modulation) -> Self` (reuses `DvbT2Modulation` from `bit_interleaver.rs`).
   - `pub fn demux(&self, bits: &BitVec) -> BitVec` — forward §6.1.4 permutation.
   - `pub fn inverse(&self, bits: &BitVec) -> BitVec` — inverse permutation for the receive path.
   - `pub fn inverse_llrs(&self, llrs: &[Llr]) -> Vec<Llr>` — LLR-domain inverse.

3. Implement the exact §6.1.4 demux per Table 11 / 11a of ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1:
   - For each modulation (QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM), apply the spec's bit-to-sub-stream demux pattern.
   - QPSK (η_MOD = 2): identity demux (per spec) — verify and document.
   - 16-QAM (η_MOD = 4): 4 sub-streams, deterministic bit-to-cell pattern from Table 11.
   - 64-QAM (η_MOD = 6): 6 sub-streams, deterministic pattern from Table 11a.

4. Unit tests:
   - Roundtrip identity: `inverse(demux(x)) == x` for random inputs at each modulation.
   - LLR-domain inverse: `inverse_llrs` reorders LLRs to match `inverse` applied to a hard-decision BitVec.
   - Spec-compliance forward test: for at least one modulation, construct an input with known bit pattern and verify the output matches a hand-derived expected pattern per the spec formula.
   - Word-boundary edge cases (0, 1, 63, 64, 65 bits offset).

## Success criteria

- [hard] Roundtrip identity holds for QPSK, 16-QAM, 64-QAM at both Normal frame (N=64800) and Short frame (N=16200).
- [hard] LLR-domain inverse preserves ordering (verified via index-tagging test).
- [hard] No new `unsafe`; satisfies `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- [hard] Public API has standard rustdoc (description, arguments, examples that compile, panics, complexity).

## Non-goals

- §6.1.5 cell interleaver (separate task; not required for TP07a per ETSI block diagram).
- QAM rotation (§6.1.7, TP8a) — separate stage.
- Time interleaver (§6.5).
- Production wiring into the BICM chain — `4cdaf1c5` consumes the demux as part of its TP07a validation; `003e4088` and `152388f4` do NOT need the demux (their FER simulation uses Gray-QAM mapping directly from the bit-interleaved stream, which is equivalent to mapping post-demux for purposes of bit-error-rate measurement).

## Spec reference

ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §6.1.4 ("Demultiplexing of bits into cell words") and Tables 11 / 11a for the per-modulation demux patterns.
